name: tab-bar
title: Tab bar
purpose: The two to five main destinations of an app, along the bottom of a phone screen, each with an icon and a text label.
whenToUse: For moving between the top-level screens of an app on a phone.
When the app has two to five such screens and every one of them exists.
As the last element in the page, so it sits at the bottom of the screen.
whenNotToUse: At 768px and wider. The bar is not shown there, so list the same destinations in the sidebar nav.
For more than five destinations. Keep the five most used and put the rest behind a menu action in the app header.
For switching between panels inside one view. Use tabs.
For an action such as New task. A destination is a screen, so use a button in the view.
For going back from a screen below a destination. Use the back link in the app header.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: 56px tall, with the destinations in equal columns across the full width. Shown only below 768px.

accessibility: Use a nav element with an aria-label, such as Main, holding one link per destination. They are links, not tabs, so they take no tab roles.
Set aria-current="page" on the link for the screen that is open, and on no other. It draws the mark and is what a screen reader announces.
Every link has a text label of one or two words. The icon is decoration and carries aria-hidden="true".
Tab moves through the destinations in order and Enter follows one. Both come from the link element.
The current destination is marked by a bar and a heavier label as well as by colour.
Keep the destinations in the same order on every screen.
The bar is sticky to the bottom of the page. Give the scrolling container scroll-padding-bottom of the bar's height, so a focused element is not hidden under it.
When the bar and the sidebar nav are both in the markup, the one that is not shown is not in the accessibility tree, so the destinations are announced once.
